info.title: SolidSeas REST service
info.description:
`solidseas serve` is a read-only HTTP service over folders an administrator configures (roots). It listens on 127.0.0.1 by default. docs/API.md section 8 is its reference.

- **Token.** Every route but `/v1/health` and `/v1/identity` needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, a token from the service's token file. Before sending it, check with `/v1/identity` that the service holds it.
- **Methods.** Every route answers GET and HEAD; HEAD does the same work and sends the headers alone. Any other method answers 405.
- **Locations.** A file or folder is named by a root id (`root`) and a `/`-separated path relative to it (`path`), both query parameters.
- **Queries.** A parameter a route does not name answers 400 `unknown_parameter`, one given twice 400 `duplicate_parameter`, and an empty value 400 `invalid_argument`: leave the parameter out instead. A query holds at most 12 fields.
- **Answers.** Every JSON answer is an envelope whose `kind` says what `data` holds, and every error one whose `error` holds a `code`. Ignore fields you do not know, and treat enumerations and error codes as open sets.
- **Caching.** An answer about a file or folder carries an `ETag`; send it back in `If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.
- **Provisional** operations and parameters (`x-solidseas-provisional`) may change in any release. The rest is stable within this API version.

get.summary: Prove the service holds a client's token
get.description:
Call it before sending a token: the answer's `proof` is the HMAC-SHA256 of the client's name, your nonce and the address and port the connection reached, keyed with the client's token. Compute the same with your token and send the token only when the two match, on the same connection. Needs no token. docs/API.md 8.16 has the exact message and clients in Python, curl, PowerShell and TypeScript.

HEAD is answered too, with the headers alone. Reference: docs/API.md section 5.12.

get.summary: List a folder's documents
get.description:
The documents and folders in a folder of a root, a page at a time, each document read in a worker process: a file that fails becomes an entry with its error and the page goes on. Entry paths are relative to the root. When a page stops at `limit` or at its deadline, `next_cursor` gives the next page: send it back as `cursor` with the other parameters unchanged.

A page has 60 s and each document 10 s by default; an answer over 8 MiB answers 422 `response_too_large`.

HEAD is answered too, with the headers alone. Reference: docs/API.md section 5.7.

parameters.name: root
parameters.description: The id of a root, as `/v1/roots` lists them.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The folder, `/`-separated and relative to the root. Leave it out for the root's own folder. A path that names a file answers 400 (rule `not_a_folder`).

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: List the subfolders too, breadth first. A root served without its subfolders answers 400. `true` or `false`; `1` and `0` are accepted too.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: What each document entry carries, replacing the default: `properties` (the active configuration's effective properties), `configurations`, `preview` (its description) and `preview_data` (the image inline, as base64).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most entries a page holds.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page, sent back as it was, with the other parameters unchanged. A cursor from another query answers 400.

parameters.name: formats
parameters.description: Provisional. The formats listed: `solidworks` (the default), `all` the formats the service reads, or comma-separated format ids among them. A format the service was not started to read answers 400. The ids SolidSeas knows: `3dxml`, `3mf`, `acis`, `alibre`, `alibre_drawing`, `alibre_package`, `amf`, `edrawings`, `fusion`, `gltf`, `iges`, `inventor`, `nx`, `obj`, `occt_brep`, `off`, `parasolid`, `ply`, `solid_edge`, `solidworks`, `step`, `stl`, `vrml`.

200.description: The `listing` envelope. A page holding an entry that may read differently later (`locked`, `timeout`) has no ETag.
